title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired Δ = 0.015; preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility (canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes in the paper and Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and to assist NetOps automation. Operational correctness demands preserving invariants and bounding blast radius (collateral network impact). A common architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes configuration candidates, a deterministic verifier checks functional and policy invariants, and an automated repair routine attempts correction when violations are detected. Prior work on tool‑assisted critiquing and verifier‑guided repair suggests potential operational benefits, but rigorous, preregistered evidence using provenance‑anchored archives is limited. We ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and average blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded multi‑vendor synthetic benchmark? Contributions: (1) a preregistered, paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3); (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle (canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) with per‑episode verifier traces and provider call artifacts; (3) confirmatory statistics (exact McNemar test and preregistered bootstrap percentile CIs) and deterministic reproduction recipes; (4) an artifact‑grounded failure analysis explaining why the preregistered efficacy threshold was not met and operational recommendations.
sections.related_work: Tool‑assisted critique and verifier insertion. Work such as CRITIC (Gou et al., 2023) formalizes tool‑interactive critiquing and motivates closed‑loop LLM pipelines. Deterministic verification and formal reachability (SymNet and model‑checking approaches) provide rigorous policy checks and reachability guarantees that are attractive for NetOps safety. Recent NetOps efforts (PreConfig, intent engines, intent translation) demonstrate LLM feasibility for configuration generation but note correctness and safety gaps that motivate verifier insertion. Surveys of LLMs for NetOps and intent translation highlight auditability, constrained repair budgets, and the risk of ceiling effects when model baseline accuracy is high. Our study is differentiated by a preregistered primary estimand, a paired within‑task design, deterministic archiving of raw responses and verifier traces, and reproducible bootstrap recipes tied to artifact checksums.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed on a deterministic validator correctness indicator. The confirmatory design targeted an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 with 200 pairs (paired design; exact McNemar two‑sided inference at α=0.05; bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Inclusion/exclusion, missingness handling, maximum repair calls per pair (1), and analytic procedures were preregistered and archived. The execution manifest records planned_episodes = 400 and completed_episodes = 376 (complete_pairs = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12); see execution/execution_manifest.json (artifact bundle). Model and orchestration. Experiments ran under adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Each pair used a single shared_initial candidate generation (shared_initial) per preregistration: the same initial LLM response was scored under both conditions to isolate verifier/repair effects. Guarded condition semantics. In the guarded condition the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 examined the shared candidate and produced structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) reporting parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and difficulty metadata. If violations were reported, the pipeline invoked at most one automated repair attempt (preregistered maximum repair calls = 1). The verifier's validity decision (valid: true/false) is the binary success indicator used in primary analysis. Synthetic benchmark and task generation. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to synthesize a Cornetto‑like multi‑vendor seeded benchmark restricted to constructs supported by the verifier. Confirmatory sampling produced 200 pairs stratified by topology scale (small/medium/large) and vendor‑mix; unsupported tasks were deterministically excluded and moved to exploratory buckets (task manifest archived: execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Missingness and sensitivity. Primary handling excluded pairs where both episodes failed ('complete_pair_primary') yielding complete_pairs = 188. A preregistered sensitivity treats both‑missing pairs as failures ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'); we report both analyses. Deterministic bootstrap reproduction (preregistered). The preregistered bootstrap uses 10,000 resamples and seed=1729. Reproduction commands (artifact‑relative paths): 1) extract per‑pair outcomes into NDJSON using the bundled extractor: python3 execution/tools/extract_pairs.py --input execution/raw_results.jsonl --output analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson 2) run the bootstrap script: python3 execution/tools/bootstrap_delta.py --input analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson --resamples 10000 --seed 1729 --output analysis/bootstrap_delta.json. The canonical raw_results.jsonl checksum is 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7; the analysis executor logged bootstrap parameters in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc). These commands deterministically reproduce the preregistered bootstrap CI reported below.
sections.results: Execution accounting and primary counts. Planned_episodes = 400; completed_episodes = 376; failed_episodes = 24; complete_pairs for primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Confirmatory contingency (complete_pairs n = 188): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded only), n_01 = 0 (baseline only), n_00 = 0 (both fail) (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766). Aggregate successes: baseline = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded = 188/188 = 1.0; paired Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered paired bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) for the complete‑pair analysis is [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records seed/resamples). Sensitivity analysis (both‑missing→failures; full 200 pairs). Treating the 12 both‑missing pairs as failures yields counts n_11 = 185, n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 12 and rates guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; paired Δ = 0.015. The preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) computed from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) is [0.0, 0.035]; this is reproducible with the two commands in Methodology. Repair invocation provenance and linkage. Repair invocations were rare (stage_counts.repair = 3) and correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). The archive contains per‑episode fields repair_provider_trace_path and repair_provider_trace_sha256 for episodes where a repair was invoked; the raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc5...) deterministically links each repair invocation to episode_id, pair_id, provider_call filename, provider_call_sha256, and final score. To extract the three repair records, run the bundled jq extraction (artifact‑relative): jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256, score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json The resulting analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json is a canonical deterministic slice of execution/raw_results.jsonl and contains the three records referenced above; its creation is reproducible from the SHA‑256 of execution/raw_results.jsonl. Blast‑radius and repair diagnostics. The verifier traces include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count; these fields permit per‑episode blast‑radius calculations (touch count and required_command_count used as compact proxies). For the three repaired episodes the verifier trace difficulty summaries indicate small dependency patterns (e.g., shutdown_configure_restore or ordering corrections) and small touched_field_count (≤4), matching low observed blast radius for the corrected cases. Repair iterations were at most one by design; stage_counts.repair = 3 indicates a small operational repair budget was sufficient for the corrected episodes but rarely invoked overall. Representative artifacts. Representative per‑task payloads, shared_initial responses, verifier traces, and scoring outcomes are archived under execution/responses/ and execution/scoring/ with checksums in the artifact bundle; see the artifact manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) and representative artifact SHA‑256s listed in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. The effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and not statistically significant at α = 0.05. Two artifact‑grounded operational drivers explain the result: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and repair budget — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and sampled tasks often produced LLM proposals that already matched golden configurations or passed validation, so repair was rarely invoked (repair invocations = 3). Threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial generation isolates verifier/repair effects but creates pairwise dependence accounted for by the preregistered paired test. Execution determinism: the study archived seeds, provider call counts, and key artifact checksums (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc5...) to permit deterministic reproduction of bootstrap CIs and repair slices. Construct validity: the success metric depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 coverage; unsupported vendor constructs were excluded deterministically from confirmatory sampling. External validity: single‑model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic task scope limit generality. Operational recommendations. (1) Where baseline correctness is high, treat verifier insertion primarily as an audit and trace generator for accountability rather than a primary mechanism for large absolute correctness gains. (2) To measure verifier impact, increase task difficulty beyond verifier coverage or enlarge repair budgets (allow multiple iterative repairs) so repairs are exercised more often. (3) Evaluate across multiple LLMs and verifiers and expand verifier coverage to vendor features encountered in production to observe richer repair dynamics.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Repairs were infrequent (3 invocations) and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We publish the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes so others can reproduce the preregistered sensitivity CI and enumerate repair invocations from the canonical archives.

Provider_call files referenced by repair_provider_trace_path live under execution/provider_calls/ in the artifact bundle and can be cross‑checked by SHA‑256. limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.
